text:
maria: FYI canary in eu-west started returning 503s after one of the canary pods was evicted during the DB migration window. Seen ~2min of errors, then fell back to stable. Thinking we should extend canary duration and add eviction backoff so we don't false-fail the rollout.

maria: Details: release=payments-proxy, chart=payments-proxy-chart, attempted upgrade 1.4.3 -> 1.5.0, canary=5% (5 pods).

alex: ugh. do we know which node got drained? logs?

maria: node drain started at 1749876520, pod rescheduled then OOMKilled once then evicted. snippet:

```
kubectl get pods -n prod | grep payments-proxy
payments-proxy-canary-7d9f  0/1 CrashLoopBackOff  1  2m

kubectl describe pod payments-proxy-canary-7d9f -> Evicted: "The node had condition: DiskPressure"
```

shiv: sounds like noisy eviction during migration window. If the canary window is short the deploy bot will mark it as failed. Proposal: extend canary.duration to 30m and add a helm value like `evictionBackoff` (2m -> 5m) so our health check tolerates transient pod restarts. Also pin chart version until post-migration.

alex: agree with extension. Quick thought — would increasing the readinessProbe initialDelay help instead of backoff? we might mask real regressions.

maria: good call. I'd prefer a short backoff + extend duration. That keeps sensitivity but avoids flapping from infra ops. Example values change I'm going to propose in the PR:

```yaml
canary:
  enabled: true
  duration: "30m"
  traffic: 5%
evictionPolicy:
  evictionBackoff: "3m"   # allow kube to reattach/evict/recreate without failing the canary
readinessProbe:
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 10
```

sre-oncall: Also recommend temporarily pinning nodeSelector to avoid nodes currently under migration if feasible, or run the extended canary in a different AZ. But pinning chart -> patch looks sane.

deploy-bot: Canary update detected: payments-proxy v1.5.0 -> canary=5% (5 pods) at 1749876500. Monitoring health.

alex: If we extend to 30m and set evictionBackoff=3m we should add a short note in release notes: "Canary extended due to infra migration; will revert to default after migration window" so product sees why rollout took longer.

maria: I'll open a hotfix PR to the release overlay with the values patch + chart pin to 1.5.0-stable and the release-notes blurb. If this repeats after extension we roll back to 1.4.3 and re-run once migration completes.

shiv: +1. tag me on the PR. Also suggest we add a small test to the canary harness to ignore single-node evictions as transient (ticket GH#1234).

alex: :thumbsup: can we do the PR and get the deploy-bot to re-evaluate?

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/pull/489 — includes values override and pinned chart version. Will request canary re-eval once merged.

deploy-bot: PR merged, canary re-eval queued.

sre-oncall: I'll watch metrics for the next 45m and report back if we see repeated 503s.

maria: thanks — will add a small note to release notes and mark this rollout as "extended canary due to infra migration" in the release tracker.
